newsitem.title: INDIA: India survey foresees over 10 pct industry growth.
newsitem.headline: India survey foresees over 10 pct industry growth.

text.p: Most Indian companies expect industrial production to rise by more than 10 percent in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March), according to a survey released on Wednesday by a leading trade body.
The survey by the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII) showed that 57 percent of the 361 companies participating in the poll forecast industrial growth to exceed 10 percent.
Twenty-two percent of the respondents said industrial growth would range between five and 10 percent. Seventeen percent forecast growth of between zero and five percent, CII said.
India's centre-left government has set a target of 12 percent growth in industrial production in 1996/97.

The index of industrial production increased by 9.3 percent during the four months from April to July compared to the same period in 1995. The growth rate in April-July 1995 over the same period in 1994 was 12.3 percent.

Of the 361 companies, CII's survey included makers of basic goods (6.7 percent of respondents), capital goods (28 percent), intermediate products (38.4 percent) and consumer goods (19.4 percent), as well as service sector firms (9.1 percent).

The survey said 38 percent of the respondents saw no change in the business trend over the next six months. Thirty-six percent foresaw a slowdown and 26 percent said they expected the business outlook to improve.
Eighty-one percent of those surveyed said the inflation rate as measured by the wholesale price index (WPI) would fluctuate between five and 10 percent.
The inflation rate as measured by the WPI stood at 6.61 percent in the week ending at November 16. The rate was 4.18 percent on June 30.
"Infrastructural constraints remain a major bottleneck affecting the overall performance of the industry," the CII's business outlook said.
Power, roads, railways and ports were seen as major infrastructure constraints.
It said "both availability of credit short term and long term as also the cost of credit, delays in sanctions and disbursements would continue to threaten the growth momentum".
Nineteen percent of those surveyed said credit would continue to be tight and hinder production growth.
About 13 percent cited orders as an impediment to increased output while power shortages and political instability were cited by 10 percent of the respondents.

Nearly 48 percent of those surveyed were "optimistic" about export prospects in 1996/97, while 36 percent expected the current trend to continue. The remaining 16 percent expected a slowdown in exports.
India's exports during April-September increased 9.91 percent over the same period in 1995. Exports grew 26.37 percent during the same six months in 1995 compared with the same period in 1994.
